steps.premise: The group may have different numbers of chairs free on different dates.
steps.action: List the available count for each date on the shared calendar.
steps.consequence: Organizers can check whether there are enough chairs for their event.
steps.quote: Put the number of available chairs against each date on a shared booking calendar so organizers can see whether a request will fit.

steps.premise: Some organizers cannot make a reservation over the internet.
steps.action: Accept telephone bookings and enter them in the same record as online bookings.
steps.consequence: People without internet access can reserve under the same conditions.
steps.quote: Take bookings by phone as well as online and enter both in the same record. Someone without internet access can reserve a set on the same terms as anyone else.

steps.premise: A chair loan may extend into the day after the event.
steps.action: Ask for pickup and return times when taking the reservation.
steps.consequence: The booking reflects when the chairs will actually be out.
steps.quote: Ask for the pickup and return times when a booking is made, since a Saturday evening event may mean the chairs are still out on Sunday morning.

steps.premise: A late driver may need to coordinate access during the event.
steps.action: Ask the organizer to name someone the driver can reach then.
steps.consequence: The driver can call the person who has the keys.
steps.quote: Have each organizer name someone reachable during the event. A driver running late can call the person with the keys.

steps.premise: Popular dates may attract requests for chairs that are already booked.
steps.action: Keep a waiting list for those dates.
steps.consequence: Organizers can register interest in chairs that become free.
steps.quote: Offer a waiting list for popular dates and ask borrowers to release surplus chairs when their head count drops.

steps.premise: A borrower who expects fewer guests may have reserved more chairs than needed.
steps.action: Ask the borrower to release the extra chairs when the guest count falls.
steps.consequence: The extra seats become available to others.
steps.quote: Offer a waiting list for popular dates and ask borrowers to release surplus chairs when their head count drops.

steps.premise: A borrower needs to know how much cargo space chairs take up alone and in stacks.
steps.action: Publish measurements for a folded chair and a stack of nested chairs.
steps.consequence: Borrowers can work out what their vehicles will hold.
steps.quote: Publish the dimensions of a folded chair and a nested stack so a borrower can work out what will fit in their vehicle.

steps.premise: A chair found after cleanup may be separated from the group that owns it.
steps.action: Put the group's name and return contact number underneath each seat.
steps.consequence: The finder can get in touch to return the chair.
steps.quote: Attach the group's name and return number under each seat, giving anyone who finds a stray chair after cleanup a way to get it home.

steps.premise: Borrowers will need to know how many chairs to gather at pack-up.
steps.action: At handover, count the chairs with the borrower and give them a copy of the tally.
steps.consequence: The borrower has the agreed count to check against when packing up.
steps.quote: Count the chairs together at handover and give the borrower a copy of the count to use when the room gets packed up.

steps.premise: Moving a load between storage and a vehicle can take several trips.
steps.action: Keep a handcart at the store entrance for borrowers.
steps.consequence: Borrowers can wheel chairs between the shelves and their vehicle.
steps.quote: Keep a handcart by the store entrance for borrowers making several trips between the shelves and a vehicle.

steps.premise: The wrong entrance can leave a volunteer carrying chairs around the building.
steps.action: Send a picture of the loading door with pickup instructions.
steps.consequence: The volunteer can go straight to the correct door.
steps.quote: Include a photo of the correct loading door with the pickup details. It can save a volunteer a walk around the building carrying chairs.

steps.premise: The people setting up the hall will need to operate the borrowed chairs.
steps.action: Show the borrower how one chair in the set opens and folds.
steps.consequence: The borrower can pass the demonstration on to the setup team.
steps.quote: Show the borrower how to open and close one chair from the set so they can demonstrate it to the people setting up the hall.

steps.premise: A defective chair might be selected for the next delivery.
steps.action: Give it a visible repair tag and store it separately.
steps.consequence: The damaged chair is kept out of the outgoing load.
steps.quote: Give a chair with a loose hinge or missing foot a conspicuous repair tag and a separate storage spot, keeping it out of the next delivery.

steps.premise: After guests leave, the organizer still has to remember to pack up the chairs.
steps.action: Remind them on the morning the return is due.
steps.consequence: Packing the chairs stays on their list for that day.
steps.quote: Send a reminder on the morning of an agreed return so packing up the chairs stays on the organizer's list after the guests leave.

steps.premise: A returned batch needs inspection and cleaning before it is collected again.
steps.action: Leave time for those tasks between reservations.
steps.consequence: The group can prepare the chairs before the next pickup.
steps.quote: Allow time between bookings to check and clean a returned batch before another group expects to collect it.

steps.premise: Some chairs may be wet when returned.
steps.action: Unfold them in a sheltered place to dry before putting them away.
steps.consequence: The chairs enter storage dry.
steps.quote: Provide a sheltered place to unfold wet returns and let them dry before they go back into storage.

steps.premise: Stacks put away in the wrong place can obstruct the storeroom door.
steps.action: Mark stack positions on the floor.
steps.consequence: A borrower can put the chairs away and leave the entrance clear.
steps.quote: Lay out parking positions for stacks on the storeroom floor so a borrower can put a load away without blocking the door.

steps.premise: Seat width and chair arms may make a borrowed chair unsuitable for a guest.
steps.action: State the width and whether chairs have arms in booking information.
steps.consequence: Hosts have time to arrange suitable alternatives for those guests.
steps.quote: Show the seat width and whether the chairs have arms in the booking information, giving hosts time to arrange other seating for guests who need it.

steps.premise: An event team may want reserved seats without sticking anything to borrowed chairs.
steps.action: Supply removable signs that clip onto rows.
steps.consequence: The team can mark reservations without leaving adhesive on the chairs.
steps.quote: Give the event team removable row signs that clip on. They can reserve seats without leaving tape or adhesive on borrowed chairs.

steps.premise: Borrowing costs or breakage charges can affect a small group's event budget.
steps.action: Set out applicable charges before the group confirms its booking.
steps.consequence: The group can plan for the expense in time.
steps.quote: Explain any charge for borrowing or breakage before confirming the booking, while a small group can still plan its budget.

steps.premise: The organizer may need to leave before the chairs can be returned.
steps.action: Allow the borrower to designate another person to return them.
steps.consequence: The chairs can still arrive by the agreed time.
steps.quote: Let a borrower nominate another person to make the return so the chairs can get back on time even when the event organizer has to leave early.

steps.premise: A single chair left at the venue can delay an otherwise complete return.
steps.action: Let the borrower report it so a volunteer can arrange a separate pickup.
steps.consequence: The rest of the chairs can be returned while the stray chair is recovered.
steps.quote: Give borrowers a simple way to report a chair left at a venue. A volunteer can arrange to recover just that chair instead of holding up the whole return.

steps.premise: Borrowers without cars may have no way to transport the chairs.
steps.action: Offer to connect them with drivers who have volunteered to help.
steps.consequence: The group can lend chairs to events that would otherwise lack transport.
steps.quote: Offer to match car-free borrowers with volunteer drivers who have already agreed to help, widening the range of events the chairs can serve.

steps.premise: Completed loans alone do not show recurrent unmet demand.
steps.action: Record unfilled requests alongside loans and look for repeated shortages on the same weekend.
steps.consequence: The group can use those shortages to guide a later purchase.
steps.quote: Record requests the group couldn't fill as well as completed loans. Repeated shortfalls on the same weekend can guide a future purchase.

steps.premise: The venue may own chairs that resemble the loaned ones.
steps.action: Check for lookalike chairs and separate the two sets into piles during cleanup.
steps.consequence: The group can avoid having to trace mistakenly exchanged chairs the next day.
steps.quote: Ask whether the venue already has folding chairs that look like ours. Sorting the two sets into separate piles during cleanup is easier than tracing a mix-up the next day.
